title: Nilpotent derived reduction detects an upper cohomological bound
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal with $I^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$, $C\in D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $b\in\mathbf Z$. Put $\overline C=C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A/I$ using derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] on the one-object site with only the identity covering. If $H^i(\overline C)=0$ for every $i>b$, then $H^i(C)=0$ for every $i>b$.

source.place: Tag 0H75, lemma-check-tor-dimension-modulo-nilpotent, upper-bound-only version of its nilpotent filtration proof, as used by Tag 09AR

proof.text: Choose a termwise flat K-flat resolution P of a representative of C. Evaluation at the sole object is an additive exact equivalence with ModuleCat A: its inverse is the constant module presheaf, every presheaf is a sheaf for the bottom topology, and the unit is the identity after identifying every site object with the sole object. The sheafification unit identifies evaluated sheaf tensor with ordinary tensor, naturally in both variables. This also identifies unbounded total tensor because the equivalence preserves coproducts. Consequently evaluation preserves termwise flatness and K-flatness.

source.place: Tag 0H75, lemma-check-tor-dimension-modulo-nilpotent, upper-bound-only version of its nilpotent filtration proof, as used by Tag 09AR

proof.text: Use derivedChangeOfRings to get a canonical derived extension whose counit is invertible on P. The supplied object and map formulas identify its additive scalar extension with E. Uniqueness of left derived functors therefore identifies LF(C) with Q(E(P)). Evaluation commutes with scalar extension: on the bottom-topology point site the sheafification unit is invertible and its evaluated source is the ordinary extension of scalars. Hence the ordinary reduced evaluated complex has zero homology above b.

source.place: Tag 0H75, lemma-check-tor-dimension-modulo-nilpotent, upper-bound-only version of its nilpotent filtration proof, as used by Tag 09AR

proof.text: Ordinary extension of scalars preserves K-flatness. For a K-flat ordinary B-complex Q with homology zero above b and any B-module M, the existing derived tensor upper-bound theorem applied to Q and M[0] gives an upper bound b+0. The K-flat tensor-single comparison identifies this derived tensor with termwise tensor. Braiding exchanges the two factors, giving vanishing for M tensor Q above b.

source.place: Tag 0H75, lemma-check-tor-dimension-modulo-nilpotent, upper-bound-only version of its nilpotent filtration proof, as used by Tag 09AR

proof.text: For a module M killed by I, use the canonical quotient-ring action. The natural balanced tensor-restriction-extension comparison identifies M tensor_A P with restriction of M tensor_B (B tensor_A P). Restriction of scalars is exact and commutes with homology, so the preceding upper bound proves the claim for all such M.

source.place: Tag 0H75, lemma-check-tor-dimension-modulo-nilpotent, upper-bound-only version of its nilpotent filtration proof, as used by Tag 09AR

proof.text: Induct on n for modules killed by I^n. The n=0 case is a zero module. For n+1, set L=IM. Powers of ideal elements and the submodule smul induction show I^n L=0, while I kills M/L. The sequence L to M to M/L is short exact. Termwise flatness of P makes its termwise tensor sequence a short exact sequence of complexes. Exactness of the homology sequence and vanishing of both outer homology objects yield vanishing of the middle one in each degree above b.

source.place: Tag 0H75, lemma-check-tor-dimension-modulo-nilpotent, upper-bound-only version of its nilpotent filtration proof, as used by Tag 09AR

proof.text: Apply the induction to M=A and exponent N, using I^N=0. The tensor unit isomorphism gives the bound for the evaluated P. The point equivalence preserves and reflects zero homology. Finally transport the bound along Q(P) isomorphic to C.

lean.statement: theorem isZero_homology_of_nilpotent_derived_reduction {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hI : I ^ N = ⊥) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (RingSiteModules A)] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (RingSiteModules (A ⧸ I))] (E : RingSiteModules A ⥤ RingSiteModules (A ⧸ I)) (hobjects : ∀ M : RingSiteModules A, E.obj M = SheafOfModules.changeOfRings (ringSiteMap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) M) (hmaps : ∀ {M M' : RingSiteModules A} (f : M ⟶ M'), E.map f = eqToHom (hobjects M) ≫ SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsHom (ringSiteMap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) M f ≫ eqToHom (hobjects M').symm) [E.Additive] (LF : DerivedCategory (RingSiteModules A) ⥤ DerivedCategory (RingSiteModules (A ⧸ I))) (ε : Qh ⋙ LF ⟶ E.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ Qh) (hLF : LF.IsLeftDerivedFunctor ε (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (RingSiteModules A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) (C : DerivedCategory (RingSiteModules A)) (b : ℤ) (hred : ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero ((homologyFunctor (RingSiteModules (A ⧸ I)) i).obj (LF.obj C))) : ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero ((homologyFunctor (RingSiteModules A) i).obj C)
